REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The Judge is Taurus's .45 Colt/.410 revolver, and Taurus covers it with its general REVOLVERS book - one manual for some sixty models. That book never prints the word Judge, so this guide uses only what the book says of every revolver it covers: open the cylinder, eject, clean with the cylinder out, and do not take the barrel off. There is no field strip beyond that, and the book says so. On a gun that fires shot shells, the cylinder and bore carry more to clean than on any other Taurus revolver.

steps.title: One book for sixty revolvers - read only what applies to all of them
steps.action: Taurus's REVOLVERS book covers your Judge but never names it. Its specification tables list several .45 LC/.410 GA revolvers by model number, and the book does not say which number is the Judge, so do not take a figure from those tables as yours.
steps.prose: The compact-frame table alone prints a '410' and '410 UL' at 45 LC/.410 GA in 3-, 4- and 6.5-inch barrels, with a separate '413' beside it, and a larger frame carries more .410 guns further on. Barrel lengths, weights and sight types differ between them. Everything in this guide is from the book's general sections, which speak to every revolver in it.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Compact Frame Fixed Sights Revolvers - specifications, printed pp.16-17 (PDF p.9)

steps.title: Check the shell length stamped on your barrel
steps.action: Before any .410 shell goes near the gun, read the chamber length marked on your own barrel and use nothing longer. The book's '410' entry does not print a shell length, so the barrel marking is the authority.
steps.prose: Judges have been built with more than one .410 chamber length, and the model name does not settle which yours is. If you cannot read the marking, a .45 Colt cartridge is always within spec. The book is blunt about the stakes in its ammunition section: the gun may fire if dropped, and the cylinder stays empty unless you are actually firing.
steps.quote:
WARNING - ANY GUN MAY FIRE IF DROPPED
If dropped or struck, the revolver may fire. Keep the cylinder empty unless actually firing!
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Ammunition, printed p.30 (PDF p.16)

steps.title: Thumb piece FORWARD, cylinder out to the left
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger off the trigger. Push the thumb piece forward with your right thumb and press the cylinder out to the left at the same time.
steps.prose: Thumb piece toward the muzzle - the opposite of what most other makers' latches do. The book's ATTENTION note adds a front latch, pressed down with the left thumb, on a short list of model numbers; if your crane has a second latch at the front of the ejector rod, press it at the same time. ⚠ The section is headed for .357 Magnum / .38 Special, and yours is neither: it is the only cylinder-opening procedure the book prints and it names no caliber-specific part, but the heading is the heading, and you should know it says that.
steps.quote: LOADING THE CYLINDER FOR .357 MAGNUM / .38 SPECIAL With the thumb of the right hand, push the thumb piece forward and at the same time press the cylinder, swinging it out to the left. ATTENTION: On Model 30, Model 218, Model 416, Model 454, Model 444, Model 45, Model 513 and Model 513UL using the left thumb, press down the front latch simultaneously.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Operating Instructions, printed p.32 (PDF p.17)

steps.title: Muzzle up, one sharp push on the extractor rod
steps.action: With the cylinder fully out, raise the muzzle and press sharply on the extractor rod. Be sure every case and hull has left the cylinder.
steps.prose: Expect harder work than on a .38. The Judge's cylinder is long and the ejector rod pushes a fired .410 hull only part of its length; swollen plastic hulls can stay put and need pulling by hand. Never lever the extractor rod sideways to help it - a bent rod is what stops a cylinder closing.
steps.quote: Cartridges are then ejected by pressing sharply on the extractor rod. Be sure that all fired cartridges are ejected. The cylinder is now ready to be reloaded.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Operating Instructions, printed p.32 (PDF p.17)
steps.warn: Spent cases will be hot and may have sharp edges. Exercise caution when removing the cases or injury may occur.

steps.title: Nothing here transfers to a look-alike
steps.action: This guide belongs to the Judge and the book it is taken from. Taurus prints the warning that look-alike firearms differ widely in the location and function of their controls.
steps.prose: Other .410 revolvers exist, and they do not all open the same way. The tell is a control that behaves the other way: if pushing the thumb piece forward does nothing, stop - you are not holding this gun.
steps.quote:
FIREARMS ARE NOT ALL ALIKE
Many makes and models of firearms might LOOK nearly the same. However, they differ widely in design, operation, and in the location and function of various controls.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Ammunition, printed p.30 (PDF p.16)

steps.title: Look AND feel every chamber - that is the working state
steps.action: Before any solvent comes out: muzzle safe, finger off the trigger, thumb piece depressed and the cylinder completely swung out, and the revolver confirmed unloaded by looking into AND feeling each chamber.
steps.prose: Both senses. A brass case head or a hull base sitting deep in a long .410 chamber reads as chamber wall at bench-light angles, and a fingertip finds what the light hides. From here the cylinder stays out - it is the only access this revolver gives you.
steps.quote: Before cleaning, (1) keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, (2) keep your finger off the trigger, (3) depress thumb piece and completely swing out the cylinder, (4) ensure the firearm is completely unloaded by looking and feeling each chamber.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: Field strip complete - the barrel stays on
steps.action: Cylinder swung out and every chamber empty. That is the whole field strip. Taurus states the revolver is cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions with no disassembly, and then says plainly: do not disassemble the barrel.
steps.prose: Where a revolver needs opening for repair, the book routes it to the factory, a qualified gunsmith or the importer. The exploded views at the back of the book are parts diagrams for ordering, with no order of operations - they are not a disassembly procedure.
steps.quote: 1. The firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly. Do not disassemble the barrel.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: Powder residue out of the barrel, lead scrubbed wet
steps.action: After shooting, remove all powder residue from the barrel and the areas around it with an appropriate brush. If you find lead particles in the barrel, scrub them with a brass brush drenched in oil, then lubricate.
steps.prose: Wet brass brush, never steel and never dry. A .410 barrel collects plastic wad streaking down the rifling and shot scrubbing lead into it, and both bake on if left - work the forcing cone and the first inches of rifling hardest, then check the bore against a light.
steps.quote: 5. For cleaning after shooting, it is of special importance that all residues of powder be removed from barrel and other adjacent areas subject to such deposits, using an appropriate brush. If particles of lead are detected in barrel they must be scrubbed with a brass brush, drenched with oil.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: Clean before further shooting past 200 rounds
steps.action: Brush every chamber full length and clean the cylinder face and the area behind the star. The book adds that after more than 200 rounds in a row the firearm should be cleaned before further shooting.
steps.prose: Unburned shot-shell powder collects in the chamber mouths and a carbon ring builds on the cylinder face; grit under the star holds it proud and the cylinder will not close on it. A hull that sticks on the next range trip usually started as residue left in the chamber on this one.
steps.quote: Once cleaned, lubrication should be done as above described. When shooting more than 200 rounds in a row, your firearm should be cleaned before further shooting.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: A lightly oiled cloth, a thin film, the crevices brushed
steps.action: Rub the revolver with a lightly oiled cloth and do the same through the bore. Remove the excess oil but leave a thin protecting film, and brush the dust out of every crevice with a small, clean brush.
steps.prose: Thin is the word that matters: oil left pooled in the frame and under the crane collects grit and burnt residue. Store the revolver away from anything that holds moisture, cloth holsters included.
steps.quote: 4. For normal cleaning of firearm not used or kept in storage for some time, it is necessary to rub it with a lightly oiled cloth. In the same way proceed with the bore of the barrel. The barrel should be clean and left free of debris. The excess oil must be removed, but a thin protecting film should remain. Also the dust should be removed from all crevices with a small, clean brush.
steps.cite:
REVOLVERS
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 4 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.40 (PDF p.21)

deepAbsentReason: The Taurus REVOLVERS book publishes no disassembly for any model it covers. Its care section (printed p.40) opens by saying the firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly, adds 'Do not disassemble the barrel.', and routes any necessary disassembly to the factory, a qualified gunsmith or the importer. The exploded views at the back are parts diagrams headed with model lists and carry no order of operations. What Taurus forbids is disassembling the barrel, not cleaning the gun - that operation is carried in this spec's prohibits field and the routine clean is published in full. Nothing deeper is walked because nothing deeper is published.

cleaning.name: BORE & FORCING CONE
tasks: Remove all powder residue from the barrel and the areas around it with an appropriate brush
Work plastic wad streaking out of the rifling - a .410 shell leaves it and it bakes on if left
If lead particles are found in the barrel, scrub them with a brass brush drenched in oil, then lubricate
Check the bore against a light before the revolver goes away

cleaning.name: CYLINDER & CHAMBERS
tasks: Brush every chamber full length and check the chamber mouths, where unburned shot-shell powder collects
Take the carbon ring off the front face of the cylinder
Push the extractor rod back and clean behind the star; grit under it holds the star proud
Wipe the crane and the frame window

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR, OIL & STORAGE
tasks: Rub the revolver with a lightly oiled cloth and do the same through the bore; remove the excess but leave a thin protecting film
Remove dust from all crevices with a small, clean brush
Keep the revolver away from materials that attract moisture or carry acidity, and avoid cloth holsters that hold damp
For long storage take extra care to protect the metal surfaces against corrosion

reassembly: Nothing was removed, so nothing is refitted. Let the extractor rod return fully before the cylinder goes home.
Close the cylinder gently until it latches - never flick it shut, which knocks the crane out of true and starts the cylinder binding.
Rotate the closed cylinder by hand through a full turn and feel the cylinder stop drop into each notch.
fncheck: With every chamber confirmed empty: the cylinder should latch under light thumb pressure with no perceptible side play; hand rotation should feel the cylinder stop engage at each notch; the hammer should hold at full cock without following; and both single and double action should reset positively when the trigger returns all the way forward. Taurus's standing advice for its revolvers is to keep the cylinder empty unless actually firing.
